reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) from a 2019 study on Al0.7CoCrFeNi directly supports all key premises: it demonstrates L12 precipitation in the FCC phase of an FCC+B2 alloy after annealing, models the strengthening as Orowan bypass, and reports a ~310 MPa yield strength increase with only a ~2% ductility reduction. However, the evidence is for a different alloy system (Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni) and does not address high-temperature (700°C) behavior, which is a critical premise of the hypothesis.
premises: L12 precipitates can form in the FCC phase of a dual-phase FCC+B2 high-entropy alloy upon low-temperature annealing
These L12 precipitates are coherent and nanoscale
The L12 precipitates strengthen the alloy via an Orowan bypass mechanism
The precipitation strengthening significantly increases yield strength with only a minor loss in ductility at room temperature
